comparison: Perfect agreement on time-varying hazard findings (C29-C30). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the non-proportional hazards methodology and findings. OpenEval provides detailed methodological assessment while peer reviewers affirm the statistical approach was appropriate.

Perfect agreement on statistical methodology (C74-C79). Both support the survival analysis approach including restricted cubic splines and multiple imputation. OpenEval provides technical validation while peer reviewers confirm analyses were appropriately done.

Strong agreement on sensitivity analyses (C41-C46, C66). Both evaluations support the robustness of findings across multiple adjustment models. OpenEval notes appropriate attenuation in Model 4, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive adjustment strategy and data quality.

Strong agreement on CVD mortality findings (C31-C35). Both support the statistical significance and sex-specific effects. OpenEval notes caution needed for multiple comparisons while peer reviewers emphasize robust associations and convincing data quality.

Strong agreement on cancer mortality findings (C36-C40). Both support the statistical associations and time-varying hazard patterns. OpenEval discusses reverse causation interpretation while peer reviewers accept the robust associations without challenging the temporal patterns.

Agreement on all-cause mortality findings (C20-C22, C24, C28). Both support the primary statistical findings including non-linear relationship and mortality risk plateau. OpenEval emphasizes spline modeling evidence while peer reviewers highlight fundamental findings with convincing data quality.

Strong agreement on cohort characteristics (C7-C10, C14-C18). Both support the descriptive statistics and sample documentation. OpenEval praises transparency including selection bias acknowledgment, while peer reviewers emphasize large sample size and data quality as strengthening credibility.

Both evaluations express uncertainty about causal interpretations (C63, C68-C69). OpenEval rates mechanistic interpretations as UNCERTAIN requiring validation, while peer reviewers explicitly question causality and suggest Mendelian randomization analysis for stronger evidence.

Agreement on SRI superiority over SD-based metrics (C47-C52, C11-C13, C59). Both support the comparative analysis and incremental predictive value. OpenEval emphasizes likelihood ratio tests, while peer reviewers highlight SRI as a novel metric providing objective circadian disruption assessment.

Agreement on accelerometry methodology (C70-C73, C11-C13). Both support the data collection approach and GGIR algorithm. OpenEval notes appropriate acknowledgment of nap detection limitation, while peer reviewers affirm objective assessment quality without challenging methodology.

Agreement on background context and circadian biology (C1-C6). Both support the foundational claims about circadian disruption and health. OpenEval validates citations to established literature, while peer reviewers note the topic is popular in sleep and circadian research.

Agreement on mechanistic literature (C53-C57). Both support the prior research linking circadian disruption to CVD and cancer pathogenesis. OpenEval emphasizes biological plausibility for observed associations, while peer reviewers accept the contextualization within existing evidence.

Agreement on contextualization of findings (C58-C60). Both support the rationale for why SRI might outperform SD-based metrics. OpenEval validates the mechanistic hypothesis about rapid changes, while peer reviewers accept the evidence supporting sleep and circadian health roles.

Agreement on study conclusions and impact (C67). Both support the overall findings despite limitations. OpenEval notes robustness while acknowledging residual confounding cannot be excluded, while peer reviewers affirm wide interest and evidence for sleep-health relationships.

Agreement on sleep duration literature context (C61-C62). Both support the established knowledge citations. OpenEval validates the rationale for investigating sleep regularity as distinct dimension, while peer reviewers accept the background without challenge.

Partial overlap on limitations (C63). OpenEval supports acknowledgment of observational study limitations, while peer reviewers specifically emphasize causality concerns and suggest additional analytical approaches like Mendelian randomization.
